report_narrative: Three of four fictional entities meet the narrowly scoped ownership condition under the supplied propagation assumptions. The fourth is below that condition on stipulated complete facts, while other sanctions nexuses and authorization remain unassessed for all four.

The calculation is limited to a stipulated OFAC ownership illustration with five direct edges and four subjects. Initial blocked status, comparable ownership, complete relevant holdings and the as-of date are assumptions of this fictional example.
F-01: ENTITY-A 60.0%, ENTITY-B 55.0%, ENTITY-C 50.0% under the fictional propagation worksheet.
F-02: All four entity rows retain NOT ASSESSED for other sanctions nexus.
F-03: ENTITY-D has 49.0% known blocked ownership; remaining holders are stipulated nonblocked.

BLOCKED-A owns 60.0% of ENTITY-A. ENTITY-A therefore becomes a propagation source for its 55.0% holding in ENTITY-B. ENTITY-C reaches 50.0% through distinct 20.0% and 30.0% blocked-source holdings. Multiplying the first chain to 33.0% would apply the wrong test.

ENTITY-D has 49.0% known blocked ownership on stipulated complete facts, below this ownership condition alone. Other sanctions nexuses, applicable restrictions, transaction facts and authorization remain unassessed for all four subjects.

SYN-001 contains the fictional seed status and complete edges. Authority references explain the scoped method; no real list search, identity resolution, license assessment or operational disposition is evidenced.

Present the propagation calculation for human sanctions review. Require actual identity, applicable authority, activity and authorization evidence before any operational decision, including for ENTITY-D.
